web_evidence.title: Preview: First Comes Love by Emily Giffin
web_evidence.note: The author’s sustained preview presents a third-person prologue about Elaine, Daniel, and the family, followed by the labeled JOSIE chapter narrated in first person.

web_evidence.title: First Comes Love by Emily Giffin — Reading Guide
web_evidence.note: In the publisher-hosted interview, Giffin says the story alternates Josie’s and Meredith’s perspectives, that she switched between their voices, and discusses writing these protagonists in first person; this establishes the main chapters’ dual first-person structure.

web_evidence.title: First Comes Love by Emily Giffin
web_evidence.note: Publishers Weekly independently reports that chapters alternate between the two sisters’ points of view, corroborating the main narrative’s dual-narrator organization when read with the first-person passages.

web_evidence.title: Review: First Comes Love by Emily Giffin
web_evidence.note: The review describes chapter-by-chapter alternation between Josie and Meredith, reproduces first-person narrative passages, and separately notes that the book begins from their mother’s view, corroborating the opening/body distinction.

person_note: The sustained body alternates between participating first-person narrators Josie and Meredith; multiple narrators using the same grammatical person yield FIRST. A third-person prologue is a brief introductory exception rather than a co-controlling base strand. The quote evidence and structural sources therefore support FIRST.
